items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Jim McNeely and I do a workshop for BMI

ctx.x: When you say it seems like you’re hot again, do you think your style of writing has changed significantly in the last few years to make you hot again, or is it something that they’re just rediscovering?

Well no what happened to me is I began to write for larger ensembles, for symphony orchestras or what they call studio orchestras or whatever. And people begin to call me because they’ve heard that I do this. A soloist will go out and have to do a pops concert with some orchestra and have no music, and so they’ll call me to provide charts. I send © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

stuff for the Metropole Orchestra, which I think is one of the best in the world as far as understanding everybody’s writing. They have every arranger in the world at one time has done a project for them and I’ve done several. I write for the Carnegie Hall Jazz Band for Jon Faddis’s group, and it goes on and on. Sometimes the phone rings and occasionally I even have to turn down work which I never did before. And I teach, I have one day a week at the Manhattan School of Music and Jim McNeely and I do a workshop…
